* [Troubleshoot missing traces](/platform/observability/troubleshooting)
* [Backend API reference](/platform/observability/api-reference)

chunks.heading: Observability Dashboard
chunks.text: This page is for developers, security teams, and operators who read traces in the ArmorIQ dashboard. You learn what each screen shows, how to find one trace, and how to read the data-quality signs. The dashboard helps you move from organization-level health to the exact policy, tool, model, or error span behind an agent operation.

chunks.heading: Open Observability
chunks.text:
Choose an organization, then open **Observability** in the dashboard navigation. The navigation has four entries:

| Entry               | What it shows                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Sessions**        | The overview and the list of recent sessions (`/dashboard/observability`)          |
| **Traces**          | A filterable list of traces (`/dashboard/observability/traces`)                    |
| **Errors**          | Errors across your agents, for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days, with a product filter |
| **Policy insights** | Policy latency, matched rules, and the tools they affect, for 7 days               |

Capture settings, quota, and alerts are on a separate page: **Settings > Observability**. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls).

chunks.heading: Refresh and reporting periods
chunks.text:
Every observability query polls over HTTP every 30 seconds. This is not streaming, so data can be up to one polling interval behind after it reaches the backend. Errors and Policy insights refresh every 5 minutes.

The Overview and the Traces list request a fixed 7-day period. The backend API accepts 1 to 90 days, but these screens have no time-range selector.

**Traces per minute** has different semantics from the other overview metrics:

* Traces per minute uses a trailing 60-minute window, bounded by the requested period.
* Sessions, traces, tokens, cost, latency, and errors use the full requested period, currently 7 days in the UI.

ArmorCodex and ArmorClaude complete turn telemetry at the end of a turn, so a session can look incomplete until the turn ends, the data is sent, and the next 30-second poll runs.

chunks.heading: 1. Overview and Sessions
chunks.text:
Route: `/dashboard/observability`

Use this screen to answer whether agents are producing telemetry and which sessions were active most recently.

The overview shows:

| Metric          | Meaning                                              |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Traces / min    | Recent trace throughput over the trailing window     |
| Sessions        | Sessions active in the reporting period              |
| Traces          | Accepted traces in the reporting period              |
| Tokens (in+out) | Input plus output tokens; the hint separates the two |
| Cost            | The reported model cost                              |
| p50 latency     | Median trace duration                                |
| p95 latency     | 95th-percentile trace duration                       |
| Errors          | Traces whose status is not `ok`                      |

The Sessions table has these columns: Session, Agent, Product, Started, Traces, Tokens, Cost, Task outcome, Technical status, and Last activity. You can filter it by service name and by instrumentation scope name. Select a row to open Session Detail.

The page also shows a **Data collection** summary with a link, **Manage in organization settings**. A session outside your plan's history shows **Outside your plan's history**.

Two actions are in the page header:

* **Find execution story** opens the lookup page. See [Find one execution](#find-one-execution).
* **Export traces** starts an encrypted export of recent traces. It shows only if you may export and read content.

Current limitations:

* The overview requests the first 50 sessions.
* The backend returns cursor metadata, but the current screen has no Load more control.
* The page has loading, empty, and retryable error states.

chunks.heading: 2. Session Detail
chunks.text:
Route: `/dashboard/observability/sessions/:id`

The header shows the session ID, the agent, the product, the input-plus-output token total, the cost, the duration, the task outcome and the technical status, the start time, and the last activity. The trace table below lists the session's traces. Select a trace to open Trace Detail.

chunks.heading: 3. Trace list
4. Trace Detail
chunks.text:
Route: `/dashboard/observability/traces/:id`

The `:id` can be the ArmorIQ trace ID or the 32-character OpenTelemetry trace ID. The dashboard treats a 32-character hexadecimal value as the OpenTelemetry ID.

The header shows the trace name, the outcome, the source, the start time, and the duration. It also shows the **Platform trace ID**, the **OpenTelemetry trace ID** (with a copy button), the service, the scope, and a link to the session. A **Technical** tag appears only when the technical status adds information.

Three tabs show the same execution:

| Tab            | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Execution**  | The outcome, cost, and timing source, then a timeline: **Policy evaluation**, **Tool executions**, **Recorded execution errors**, and the **Intent plan** with each plan item, its status, its retries, and its policy decision     |
| **Operations** | Typed facts for approvals, delegations, unsuccessful operations, Bash and CLI work, MCP calls, and tool calls. Bash and CLI work shows executable names only. It never shows command text.                                          |
| **Span tree**  | The spans as a tree. Each row shows the name, status, category (Model, Policy, Approval, Delegation, Tool, MCP, Bash, CLI, Command, Plan, Error, or Event), duration, and redaction state. Select a span for its captured metadata. |

chunks.heading: Policy denial and execution failure
chunks.text: The dashboard keeps these apart. A policy result is shown in **Policy evaluation**, with the policy ID, version, rule, action, reason code, and source. A denied result is marked with a lock. A failure while a tool ran is shown in **Recorded execution errors**, with the error type and exit code. The trace outcome shows **Denied** when policy denied the run. Plan state and technical status also stay apart from the task outcome: **Completed**, **Partially completed**, **Denied**, **Failed**, **Abandoned**, or **Unknown**.

chunks.heading: Read the data-quality signs
chunks.text:
A box named **Execution data notice** and a row of quality facts tell you how far to trust the view:

| Sign                                                                        | Meaning                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "This execution story is incomplete"                                        | The trace is partial. A reason follows. See [Incomplete traces](/platform/observability/troubleshooting#incomplete-traces). |
| "Showing X of Y plan items", "The span tree is limited to N captured spans" | The view is capped. The data is stored.                                                                                     |
| "Telemetry arrived late"                                                    | The data arrived more than one minute after the run ended                                                                   |
| Source and Mapper                                                           | Where the trace came from, and the version of the mapper that read it                                                       |
| Sampling                                                                    | The sampling state, and the rate when there is one                                                                          |
| Redaction                                                                   | How many spans are in each redaction state                                                                                  |
| Capture mode and Content status                                             | The capture mode that applied, and whether content was stored                                                               |
| Pipeline health                                                             | `delayed`, `partial`, or `on time`                                                                                          |
| Rejected spans (trace-specific)                                             | A count, or "not trace-attributed" when ArmorIQ cannot tie rejections to this trace                                         |

chunks.heading: Captured content
chunks.text: The **Captured prompt and response** panel shows content only if your organization captured it and you have the content read permission. It can show **User prompt**, **Agent output**, **Tool arguments**, **Tool result**, and **Safe error summary**. Each has a **Copy** button. When content is missing, a notice says why, for example "The organization capture mode is metadata; it did not store prompt or output content." See [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture). Without the permission, you see a **Permission required** page, and metadata still shows in the lists.

chunks.heading: Find one execution
chunks.text:
Route: `/dashboard/observability/traces/find`

Open **Find execution story** to look up an execution by one field at a time: **Session ID**, **Conversation ID**, **Workflow run ID**, **Agent ID**, **Product**, or **RIS ticket ID**. To look up by ArmorIQ trace ID or OpenTelemetry trace ID, open the trace directly from its ID.

chunks.heading: Missing values and zero values
chunks.text:
Optional values render as `--` or **Not reported** when the data has no value. Timing that ArmorIQ cannot check shows as "client-reported" or "Legacy timing—not verified". Cost shows **Not reported** when it is missing, explicitly not reported, or a legacy zero.

Token and cost totals can still be zero in an aggregate when no model span reported usage. A zero can mean no model span, pricing not available, or a measured zero. Open the trace and check its model spans and token fields before you read the aggregate.

Next: [understand every field](/platform/observability/data-model), [use the read API](/platform/observability/api-reference), or [troubleshoot missing data](/platform/observability/troubleshooting).

chunks.heading: What Data Is Captured
chunks.text: This page is for security teams, administrators, and developers who must know what trace data contains. You get one table of what each capture mode records, a list of data that is always removed, and the rules for data that leaves ArmorIQ.

chunks.heading: The four capture modes
chunks.text:
Your organization sets one capture mode. It controls how much data ArmorIQ keeps from new traces. An administrator changes it in **Settings > Observability**. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls).

| Mode       | Plain meaning                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `off`      | ArmorIQ keeps no new trace data.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `metadata` | ArmorIQ keeps the shape of the run, policy decisions, status, timing, token counts, and safe error types. It keeps no prompts, no completions, and no tool inputs or outputs. This is the default. |
| `enhanced` | Same as `metadata`, plus short, redacted summaries of prompts, completions, tool arguments, and tool results. The organization must also allow content capture.                                    |
| `debug`    | Same as `enhanced`, with larger limits. It is temporary. It ends by itself within 24 hours.                                                                                                        |

A mode in an SDK or in a narrower scope can only lower the data you keep. It can never raise it above the organization setting.

chunks.heading: What each mode records
chunks.text:
| Data                                                                                                                                      | `off`         | `metadata`    | `enhanced`                | `debug`                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Any new trace or span                                                                                                                     | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Trace and span IDs, parent links, span names, start and end times, status                                                                 | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Session ID, agent ID, conversation ID, workflow ID, ticket ID                                                                             | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Policy decision, policy ID and name, policy version, rule ID, reason code, enforcement action, policy source                              | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Model name, model provider, input tokens, output tokens, cache tokens                                                                     | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Cost (ArmorIQ computes it at ingest from its own price catalog and ignores a cost that an SDK sends)                                      | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Tool name, tool type, MCP server name, tool call ID, operation category (tool, MCP, Bash, CLI, command, approval, delegation)             | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| For Bash and CLI work: executable name only, exit code, retry count, timeout and killed flags, size of standard output and standard error | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Error type (the class name) and a short error code                                                                                        | No            | Yes           | Yes                       | Yes                                           |
| Prompt text and model output text                                                                                                         | No            | No            | Yes, redacted and bounded | Yes, redacted and bounded                     |
| Tool arguments and tool results                                                                                                           | No            | No            | Yes, redacted and bounded | Yes, redacted and bounded                     |
| Error message summary (no stack trace)                                                                                                    | No            | No            | Yes, redacted and bounded | Yes, redacted and bounded                     |
| Size limit for each content field                                                                                                         | None          | None          | 2 KiB from the SDK        | 8 KiB from the SDK                            |
| How long the mode lasts                                                                                                                   | Until changed | Until changed | Until changed             | Up to 24 hours, then it returns to `metadata` |

Three rules decide whether content is stored in `enhanced` and `debug`. All three must be true:

1. The organization mode is `enhanced` or `debug`.
2. The organization allows content capture. If it does not, the effective mode is `metadata`, even when the mode says `enhanced` or `debug`.
3. For `debug`, the debug window has not ended.

Bash and CLI work has no field for the command text. Only the executable name is stored as a field. The command text can reach storage only as part of tool arguments or tool results, and only in `enhanced` or `debug`.

ArmorIQ also stamps each stored span with the capture mode and policy revision that applied to it.

chunks.heading: Fields that are always forbidden
chunks.text:
These rules apply in every mode. The SDK removes this data before it exports a span. The ArmorIQ backend removes it again when it receives a span, and the backend applies the full list below. Nobody can switch secret capture on.

| Category                                            | Examples that are removed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Credentials and secrets                             | API keys and tokens that start with `ak_`, `sk_`, `pk_`, `rk_`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `github_pat_`, `xox` (Slack), `AIza` (Google), `AKIA` or `ASIA` (AWS); JWTs; `Bearer` tokens; private key blocks (`-----BEGIN`); long random strings that mix letters and digits; text such as `password=`, `api_key:`, `authorization:`, or `cookie:` followed by a value |
| Authentication headers and cookies                  | Any attribute or object key that names an API key, authorization, bearer token, cookie, credential, password, secret, private key, token, signature, or session ID has its value removed or replaced                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Personal identifiers                                | Email addresses; US Social Security numbers and EINs; India PAN numbers; payment card numbers that pass the Luhn check; phone-like numbers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Other sensitive text                                | Statements of student grades                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Stack traces and raw error bodies                   | Only the error type and a bounded message summary are kept                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Producer-supplied authority fields                  | The backend drops cost, timing-trust, and pricing-source values that an SDK sends, and computes its own                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Any attribute that is not on the ArmorIQ allow-list | The backend drops it. It does not reject the span.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

When a value contains a forbidden match, ArmorIQ replaces the **whole value** with a marker such as `[REDACTED]` or `[REDACTED:CREDENTIAL]`. It does not cut out only the match. One match anywhere in a prompt or a tool argument replaces that whole content field.

<Callout type="warn">
  Redaction is pattern based. It cannot find a secret that matches none of the patterns, for example a password written in plain words inside a prompt. Do not place secrets in prompts or tool arguments.
</Callout>

chunks.heading: How content is bounded
chunks.text:
* Content is redacted first and cut to size second.
* The SDK limits each content field to 2 KiB in `enhanced` and 8 KiB in `debug`. It also limits nesting depth (4 and 8), items in a list (20 and 100), and the length of one string (512 and 2,048 characters).
* ArmorIQ then keeps at most 4,096 bytes of each content field when it stores the span.
* Text that is cut gets a `[TRUNCATED]` marker, and the span carries `armoriq.content.truncated`.
* Text fields that are not content (such as names and labels) are limited to 256 characters.

chunks.heading: Why a content field can be empty
chunks.text:
When content is missing, the span says why. The span has a state for each content field, and a reason code:

| Reason code                     | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `captured`                      | The content was recorded.                                                                     |
| `capture_mode_off`              | The organization mode is `off`.                                                               |
| `capture_mode_metadata`         | The mode is `metadata`, which records no content.                                             |
| `organization_content_disabled` | The mode allows content, but the organization has not allowed content capture.                |
| `external_content_disabled`     | You export to an external destination, and the organization has not allowed external content. |
| `policy_expired`                | The debug window or the policy lease ended.                                                   |
| `policy_unavailable`            | The SDK could not read the organization policy, so it kept no content.                        |
| `not_provided_by_adapter`       | The framework did not give the SDK this content, for example because no goal was passed.      |

chunks.heading: What leaves ArmorIQ when you export
chunks.text:
If you choose `external` or `provider` in [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership), spans go to a system that ArmorIQ does not control.

* **Your ArmorIQ API key never goes to an external destination.**
* **Content leaves only when all of these are true:** the effective mode is `enhanced` or `debug`; the organization allows content capture; the organization **also** allows external content capture; and the SDK holds a current organization policy. If any one is false, the SDK exports metadata only.
* **A provider that you own never receives content.** In `provider` mode the SDK limits capture to `metadata`.
* **The TypeScript SDK exports only an allow-list of attributes.** The list covers the trace structure, safe model and token attributes, and the IDs that link spans (such as the tool call ID and the plan item ID). Values that contain a credential, an email address, or a phone-like, SSN-like, or card-like number are dropped.
* **The Python SDK does not use an allow-list.** It removes ArmorIQ content keys and applies the same redaction. Its spans still carry ArmorIQ IDs such as `armoriq.session_id` and `armoriq.agent_id` to the external destination.
* **Resource attributes** such as `service.name` are cleaned before export. Do not put secrets or user content in them.

Data that you export is outside ArmorIQ access control. The destination has its own access rules. ArmorIQ cannot take back data after it leaves. See [What the dashboard Off setting does](/platform/observability/organization-controls#what-the-off-setting-does-and-does-not-do).

chunks.text:

chunks.heading: Data Model and Schema
chunks.text:
This page is for developers who read ArmorIQ trace data, build reports on it, or check what a span can hold. You get the span names, the attributes that ArmorIQ stores, and how status, outcome, tokens, and cost work.

ArmorIQ receives OpenTelemetry spans over OTLP and stores them in a normalized form. Older SDKs used a different JSON record. Its fields are at the end of this page under [Legacy JSON records](#legacy-json-records).

chunks.heading: Identifiers
chunks.text:
| Identifier                             | Format                               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Trace ID                               | 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters | The standard OpenTelemetry trace ID. ArmorIQ keeps it unchanged.                                                                                                          |
| Span ID                                | 16 lower-case hexadecimal characters | The standard OpenTelemetry span ID                                                                                                                                        |
| Session ID                             | UUID                                 | The attribute `armoriq.session_id`. The SDK uses a valid `session_id` that you pass, then a valid `context_id`, then a new UUID.                                          |
| Agent ID                               | Free-form string                     | The attributes `armoriq.agent_id` and `gen_ai.agent.name`                                                                                                                 |
| Conversation, workflow, and ticket IDs | Safe identifier strings              | `armoriq.conversation_id`, `armoriq.workflow_id`, `armoriq.ris_ticket_id`                                                                                                 |
| Plan and plan item IDs                 | Safe identifier strings              | `armoriq.intent_plan_id`, `armoriq.intent_plan_item_id`, with `armoriq.intent_plan_item_ordinal`, `armoriq.intent_plan_item_status`, and `armoriq.intent_plan_item_count` |
| Tool call ID                           | Safe identifier string               | `armoriq.tool.call_id`. The policy span and the tool span of one call share it.                                                                                           |

ArmorIQ never takes the organization, product, or user from span attributes. It takes them from your API key.

In the dashboard, open a trace by its ArmorIQ trace ID or by its 32-character OpenTelemetry trace ID. You can also look up a trace by session, conversation, workflow run, agent, product, or ticket.

chunks.heading: Span names and operation categories
chunks.text:
The SDKs use these span names:

| Span name                                        | Meaning                         |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `armoriq.agent.run`                              | The root span of a session      |
| `armoriq.intent.plan`                            | The plan that the agent made    |
| `armoriq.policy.evaluate`                        | One policy decision             |
| `gen_ai.chat`                                    | One model call                  |
| `armoriq.tool`                                   | A tool call                     |
| `mcp.execute`                                    | An MCP tool call                |
| `bash.execute`, `cli.execute`, `command.execute` | Shell and command work          |
| `armoriq.approval.wait`                          | A wait for a human approval     |
| `armoriq.delegation.wait`                        | A wait for a delegated decision |

<Callout type="info">
  Use the attribute `armoriq.operation.category` to group and filter operations. A span name is only a hint. One SDK can merge command spans, and another can keep `bash.execute`, `cli.execute`, and `command.execute` apart. The category values are `tool`, `mcp`, `bash`, `cli`, `command`, `approval`, `delegation`, and `policy`.
</Callout>

chunks.heading: Attributes that ArmorIQ stores
chunks.text:
ArmorIQ keeps a fixed list of attributes. It drops any other attribute and does not reject the span. SDKs can send more attributes than the list, such as the model finish reason, but ArmorIQ does not store them.

| Group                      | Attributes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Resource                   | `service.name`, `service.version`, `service.namespace`, `deployment.environment`, `deployment.environment.name`, `telemetry.sdk.language`, `telemetry.sdk.name`, `telemetry.sdk.version`, `cloud.provider`, `cloud.region`, `host.name`, `os.type`                                   |
| Model (GenAI)              | `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model`, `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.cache_read_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.cache_write_tokens`                                                            |
| Agent and tool             | `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `armoriq.tool.name`, `armoriq.tool.type`, `armoriq.tool.outcome`, `armoriq.mcp.server`, `armoriq.tool.call_id`, `armoriq.operation.category`                                                                                                |
| Policy                     | `armoriq.policy.id`, `armoriq.policy.name`, `armoriq.policy.version`, `armoriq.policy.decision`, `armoriq.policy.rule_id`, `armoriq.policy.reason_code`, `armoriq.policy.enforcement_action`, `armoriq.policy.default_action`, `armoriq.policy.source`                               |
| Execution                  | `process.executable.name`, `armoriq.command.exit_code`, `armoriq.execution.status`, `armoriq.execution.retry_count`, `armoriq.execution.timeout`, `armoriq.execution.killed`, `armoriq.output.stdout_bytes`, `armoriq.output.stderr_bytes`, `armoriq.output.truncated`, `error.type` |
| Approval, delegation, task | `armoriq.approval.outcome`, `armoriq.approval.wait_ms`, `armoriq.delegation.id`, `armoriq.delegation.outcome`, `armoriq.task.outcome`, `gen_ai.task.outcome`                                                                                                                         |
| Capture diagnostics        | `armoriq.observability.capture.mode`, `armoriq.observability.policy.revision`, `armoriq.observability.native_span.state`, `armoriq.observability.redaction.applied`, `armoriq.observability.content.truncated`, and a `state` and `reason_code` for each content field               |
| Content (gated)            | `armoriq.content.input`, `armoriq.content.output`, `armoriq.content.tool_arguments`, `armoriq.content.tool_result`, `armoriq.content.error_summary`, `armoriq.content.truncated`. See [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture).                                 |

ArmorIQ also adds `armoriq.observability.capture.mode` and `armoriq.observability.policy.revision` to every stored span, so that you can see which policy applied.

Some values can only be certain safe strings. For example, `armoriq.operation.category` accepts only the values above, and a free-text value that looks sensitive is dropped.

chunks.heading: Status, outcome, and policy decisions
chunks.text:
ArmorIQ keeps three things apart. Do not read one as another.

| Question                        | Where to look                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Did the technical work succeed? | The span status, and `armoriq.execution.status`                                                                            |
| Did the agent reach its goal?   | `armoriq.task.outcome`. The values are `completed`, `failed`, `denied`, `abandoned`, `partially_completed`, and `unknown`. |
| What did policy decide?         | `armoriq.policy.decision` and `armoriq.policy.enforcement_action` on the policy span                                       |

* A policy span for a deny or a hold ends with a normal span status. Only an error while the policy ran makes it an error. This keeps a policy **denial** apart from a policy **execution failure**.
* When a run ends, the SDK sets the task outcome from the run status: `ok` becomes `completed`, `error` becomes `failed`, `denied` becomes `denied`, and `cancelled` becomes `abandoned`.
* `unknown` means that the agent did not report how the task ended. The dashboard shows it as **Unknown**.
* `error.type` holds only the class name of an error. Stack traces are never stored.

chunks.heading: Timing and cost
chunks.text:
* **Timing.** A span has a start time and an end time. The SDK marks how it got them: measured in a start and end hook, reported by the caller, or recorded after the fact. ArmorIQ does not trust a timing label that an SDK sends. It sets its own label, and the dashboard shows timing it cannot check as "client-reported" or "Legacy timing—not verified".
* **Tokens.** Model spans carry input, output, cache-read, and cache-write token counts.
* **Cost.** ArmorIQ computes model cost when it receives the span, from its own price catalog. It ignores a cost that an SDK sends. The current Python SDK (0.8.17) carries no local price table. When no cost is known, the dashboard shows **Not reported**.
* Cost is best-effort and is not billing-grade.

Session totals, trace-list totals, summary metrics, and model- or session-grouped token analytics add up the tokens of model spans. Backend aggregations scan at most 50,000 rows. Results at the cap are approximate and produce a server warning.

chunks.heading: Completeness, sampling, and mapper version
chunks.text:
Every stored trace carries quality information. The dashboard and the API return it:

| Field                                                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `completenessStatus` and `completionReason`                    | Whether the trace is complete, partial, in progress, timed out, unknown, or not applicable. See [Incomplete traces](/platform/observability/troubleshooting#incomplete-traces). |
| `expectedPlanItems`, `terminalPlanItems`, `missingParentCount` | The counts that completeness uses                                                                                                                                               |
| `partial`                                                      | `true` when the trace is not complete, or when ArmorIQ capped the spans or plan items that it shows                                                                             |
| `redactionStates`                                              | The number of spans in each redaction state, such as `metadata_only` and `redacted_content`                                                                                     |
| Capture                                                        | The capture mode and policy revision that applied to the trace                                                                                                                  |
| Sampling                                                       | `retained`, `sampled_in`, or `sampled_out`, with a rate and a reason. ArmorIQ always retains traces with an error, a denial, an approval, a delegation, or a policy decision.   |
| Mapper version                                                 | `otel/v1` for OTLP spans, and `armor-sdk/v1` for the legacy JSON route                                                                                                          |

chunks.heading: Sensitive content
chunks.text:
Prompts, completions, tool arguments, and tool results are not stored in the default `metadata` mode. In `enhanced` and `debug`, they are stored only after redaction, cut to a size limit, and only when your organization allows content capture. Secrets, credentials, authentication headers, and personal identifiers are removed in every mode.

Redaction finds patterns. It cannot find every secret. Record only what you need, do not put secrets in prompts or tool arguments, and limit access to the organization-scoped read API and dashboard. See [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture) for the rules.

chunks.heading: Legacy JSON records
chunks.text:
Older SDKs sent sessions, traces, and spans as a JSON record to `POST /observability/spans`. ArmorIQ still accepts that route for a limited time, and it stores those records next to OpenTelemetry traces. See [Migrate from the legacy recorder](/platform/observability/migration). The fields below describe that record. The current SDKs (Python 0.8.17, TypeScript 0.8.23) do not send it.

```text
Session
└── Trace
    ├── span
    ├── policy_call
    ├── generation
    └── event
```

All IDs used for a trace, span, parent span, session, or user must be UUIDs when present. `agentId` is a free-form string.

chunks.heading: Session
chunks.text:
A session groups a continuous agent run or conversation. The backend creates or updates the session when it ingests a trace with a session ID.

| Field                   | Type              | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                    | UUID              | Stable session identifier                                                                |
| `orgId`                 | UUID              | Organization resolved from the API key                                                   |
| `userId`                | UUID or `null`    | User identity when the producer has a UUID                                               |
| `agentId`               | string or `null`  | Agent identifier; not restricted to UUID format                                          |
| `product`               | string or `null`  | Producer identity, such as `armoriq-sdk`, `armorcodex`, or `armorclaude`                 |
| `startedAt`             | ISO 8601 datetime | Earliest trace start recorded for the session                                            |
| `lastActivityAt`        | ISO 8601 datetime | Latest trace activity recorded for the session                                           |
| `traceCount`            | integer           | Number of accepted traces in the session                                                 |
| `totalInputTokens`      | integer           | Sum from accepted generation spans                                                       |
| `totalOutputTokens`     | integer           | Sum from accepted generation spans                                                       |
| `totalCacheReadTokens`  | integer           | Sum of reported cache-read tokens                                                        |
| `totalCacheWriteTokens` | integer           | Sum of reported cache-write tokens                                                       |
| `totalCostUsd`          | number            | Sum of reported or SDK-estimated generation cost                                         |
| `status`                | string            | Current session status; current values are `active`, `completed`, `expired`, and `error` |

The ingest path currently creates sessions with `active` status. Status changes require another backend lifecycle path; do not infer completion solely from the absence of new traces.

chunks.heading: Trace
chunks.text:
A trace is the top-level record for one IAP plan or logical operation.

| Field        | Type                           | Required | Meaning                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------ | :------: | ----------------------------------------- |
| `id`         | UUID                           |    Yes   | Trace identifier and duplicate-ingest key |
| `sessionId`  | UUID or `null`                 |    No    | Parent session                            |
| `name`       | string, 1–200 chars            |    Yes   | Operation name, commonly `iap.plan`       |
| `startTime`  | ISO 8601 datetime              |    Yes   | Trace start                               |
| `endTime`    | ISO 8601 datetime or `null`    |    No    | Trace end                                 |
| `durationMs` | non-negative integer or `null` |    No    | Total trace duration                      |
| `status`     | `ok`, `error`, or `denied`     |    Yes   | Terminal trace status                     |
| `userId`     | UUID or `null`                 |    No    | User identity                             |
| `agentId`    | string or `null`               |    No    | Agent identity                            |
| `attributes` | object                         |    Yes   | Producer-defined trace metadata           |
| `tags`       | string array                   |    Yes   | Search and summary labels                 |

The backend adds `product` and `source` to trace-detail responses. Trace-list and session-detail responses also add token totals, cost, span count, error count, and input/output previews.

chunks.heading: Span
chunks.text:
A span is one observation inside a trace.

| Field          | Type                           | Required | Meaning                                     |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ | :------: | ------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | UUID                           |    Yes   | Span identifier                             |
| `parentSpanId` | UUID or `null`                 |    No    | Parent span; `null` means a root-level span |
| `sessionId`    | UUID or `null`                 |    No    | Denormalized session identifier             |
| `kind`         | span kind                      |    Yes   | Selects the attribute schema                |
| `name`         | string, 1–200 chars            |    Yes   | Operation name                              |
| `startTime`    | ISO 8601 datetime              |    Yes   | Span start                                  |
| `endTime`      | ISO 8601 datetime or `null`    |    No    | Span end                                    |
| `durationMs`   | non-negative integer or `null` |    No    | Span duration                               |
| `status`       | `ok`, `error`, or `denied`     |    Yes   | Span status                                 |
| `attributes`   | object                         |    Yes   | Kind-specific attributes                    |

Spans are returned as a flat list. Build the tree by matching each `parentSpanId` to another span's `id`. A missing or `null` parent is a root.

chunks.heading: Span kinds and attributes
chunks.text: Attribute objects include a `kind` field matching the span's `kind`. Producers may add extra attributes; the backend preserves them.

chunks.heading: `span`
chunks.text:
Generic operation, commonly a tool call, report, dispatch, delegation, or container operation.

| Attribute      | Type                |
| -------------- | ------------------- |
| `kind`         | `span`              |
| `toolName`     | optional string     |
| `toolInput`    | optional JSON value |
| `toolOutput`   | optional JSON value |
| `errorMessage` | optional string     |

Some producer-created generic spans use additional keys such as `input`, `output`, `status`, `trustId`, or `fired`.

chunks.heading: `policy_call`
chunks.text:
Policy evaluation and its enforcement result.

| Attribute           | Type                                                            |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`              | `policy_call`                                                   |
| `policyId`          | string or `null`                                                |
| `policyName`        | string or `null`                                                |
| `policyHash`        | string or `null`                                                |
| `policyVersion`     | string or `null`                                                |
| `decision`          | `allow`, `deny`, `hold`, or `ask`                               |
| `matchedRuleId`     | string or `null`                                                |
| `dataClasses`       | string array                                                    |
| `reason`            | string or `null`                                                |
| `input`             | JSON value                                                      |
| `output`            | JSON value                                                      |
| `source`            | `native`, `sdk-local`, `sdk`, `proxy`, `opa`, or `opa_fallback` |
| `enforcementAction` | `allow`, `allow_log`, `hold`, `block`, or `null`                |
| `obligations`       | JSON value                                                      |
| `delegationId`      | string or `null`                                                |

`decision` describes the policy result. `enforcementAction` describes what the integration did with that result.

SDK recorders map `allow` to span status `ok`. They map `deny`, `hold`, and `ask` to span status `denied`.

chunks.heading: `generation`
chunks.text:
Model call and token usage.

| Attribute          | Type                           |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| `kind`             | `generation`                   |
| `model`            | string                         |
| `inputTokens`      | non-negative integer           |
| `outputTokens`     | non-negative integer           |
| `cacheReadTokens`  | non-negative integer or `null` |
| `cacheWriteTokens` | non-negative integer or `null` |
| `costUsd`          | non-negative number            |
| `prompt`           | string or `null`               |
| `completion`       | string or `null`               |
| `finishReason`     | string or `null`               |

chunks.heading: `event`
chunks.text:
Point-in-time annotation.

| Attribute | Type                       |
| --------- | -------------------------- |
| `kind`    | `event`                    |
| `message` | string                     |
| `level`   | `info`, `warn`, or `error` |

An event's `level` is the event severity. Current SDK recorders keep the event span's lifecycle `status` as `ok`, including for `level: "error"`; use the attributes and surrounding trace status when interpreting an error event.

chunks.heading: Example trace
chunks.text:
```json
{
  "id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "sessionId": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
  "name": "iap.plan",
  "startTime": "2026-07-17T09:00:00.000Z",
  "endTime": "2026-07-17T09:00:00.240Z",
  "durationMs": 240,
  "status": "ok",
  "userId": null,
  "agentId": "support-agent",
  "attributes": {
    "input": "Find the account owner"
  },
  "tags": ["armoriq-sdk", "search_contacts", "allowed"],
  "spans": [
    {
      "id": "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333",
      "parentSpanId": null,
      "sessionId": "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222",
      "kind": "policy_call",
      "name": "policy.evaluate",
      "startTime": "2026-07-17T09:00:00.010Z",
      "endTime": "2026-07-17T09:00:00.030Z",
      "durationMs": 20,
      "status": "ok",
      "attributes": {
        "kind": "policy_call",
        "policyId": "contacts-read",
        "policyName": "Contacts read policy",
        "policyHash": null,
        "policyVersion": null,
        "decision": "allow",
        "matchedRuleId": "allow-support",
        "dataClasses": [],
        "reason": "Support agents may read contacts",
        "input": { "toolName": "search_contacts" },
        "output": null,
        "source": "sdk",
        "enforcementAction": "allow",
        "obligations": null,
        "delegationId": null
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

chunks.heading: Tags and previews
chunks.text:
SDK trace summaries can derive tags from the product, tool names, and the policy outcome, such as `allowed`, `blocked`, or `mixed`. Tags are producer-supplied and are not guaranteed on every trace.

Trace-list previews prefer `trace.attributes.input` and `trace.attributes.output`. If those are absent, the backend falls back to input/output on a root span when available.

chunks.heading: Framework Support
chunks.text:
This page is for developers who choose an agent framework, and for teams that review what ArmorIQ can trace. You get the tested versions, the guarantees about when a trace ends, how ArmorIQ treats spans that the framework or another tool already creates, and the known limits.

<Callout type="info">
  A version range in a package setting is not a promise of support. Only the versions in the **Tested version** column were run against the real framework by the ArmorIQ test suites. Other versions can work. Test the exact versions in your own application before you rely on tracing.
</Callout>

chunks.heading: Support matrix
chunks.text:
| Framework              | Python                                                                             | TypeScript                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| LangChain              | Supported. Tested: `langchain` 1.2.15, `langchain-core` 1.2.31.                    | Supported. Tested: `@langchain/core` 1.2.4 (Node.js 20 or later).      |
| LangGraph              | **No version is tested.** Uses the LangChain callback path.                        | **No version is tested.** Uses the LangChain callback path.            |
| Strands Agents         | Supported. Tested: `strands-agents` 1.54.0. The package allows `>=1.54.0,<1.55.0`. | Supported. Tested: `@strands-agents/sdk` 1.11.2 (Node.js 20 or later). |
| Google ADK             | Supported. Tested: `google-adk` 1.14.1.                                            | Supported. Tested: `@google/adk` 0.6.1.                                |
| CrewAI                 | **Not supported yet** for tracing.                                                 | Not available.                                                         |
| Direct OpenAI calls    | Supported. Tested: `openai` 2.32.0. Streaming is **not** traced.                   | Supported. Tested: `openai` 6.49.0. Streaming is traced.               |
| Direct Anthropic calls | Supported. Tested: `anthropic` 0.96.0. Streaming is **not** traced.                | Supported. Tested: `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.111.0. Streaming is traced.   |

The SDK package settings allow wider ranges than the tested versions. The settings are `langchain-core>=0.2.0`, `google-adk>=1.0.0`, `openai>=1.0.0`, and `anthropic>=0.20.0` for Python, and `openai >=4.0.0` and `@anthropic-ai/sdk >=0.51.0` for TypeScript. Versions below the tested ones are not tested.

chunks.heading: What every supported adapter does
chunks.text:
For LangChain, Strands, and Google ADK, you add the ArmorIQ adapter once. See [LangChain](/sdk/integrations/langchain), [Strands](/sdk/integrations/strands), and [Google ADK](/sdk/integrations/google-adk). You then add no span code, no trace ID code, and no flush code. The adapter gives you these guarantees:

* **One connected trace per run.** A run that calls tools and a run that calls no tools both produce one trace. It has a root span, a plan span, and child spans for policy decisions, model calls, and tool calls.
* **The trace ends one time.** The adapter ends it when the run succeeds, fails, is cancelled, or is denied by policy. If the framework sends more than one end event, the extra events do nothing.
* **A short, fixed wait at the end.** The SDK waits a bounded time for spans to send. It never waits without a limit.
* **Your own callbacks stay.** The adapter adds its hooks next to yours. It does not remove them. For Google ADK, it wraps your callbacks and puts the originals back when you uninstall.
* **Runs do not mix.** Concurrent users and concurrent runs keep separate context and identity.
* **Telemetry is fail-open.** A tracing error never changes the result of the agent or a policy decision.

chunks.heading: Native spans and duplicate spans
chunks.text:
A **native span** is a span that the framework or another tool, such as OpenInference, already creates for the same model call or tool call.

* **ArmorIQ always sends its own spans.** It sends its own model, tool, and policy spans to its own destination. Another tool would send its spans to a different destination. If ArmorIQ stopped its own spans, ArmorIQ would receive no data for the call.
* **ArmorIQ never changes a native span.** It does not attach to it, reuse it, or write ArmorIQ attributes onto it.
* **ArmorIQ detects OpenInference for LangChain.** When `openinference-instrumentation-langchain` (Python) or `@arizeai/openinference-instrumentation-langchain` (TypeScript, tested at 4.1.1) is active, ArmorIQ writes `armoriq.observability.native_span.state = coexisting` once on the root span. If it is not active, the value is `emitted`. The value tells you whether two tools trace the same run.
* **ArmorIQ does not detect other tools.** LangSmith and other instrumentors cannot be detected today. ArmorIQ still sends its own spans next to theirs.
* **ArmorIQ avoids two spans for one model call.** Inside a LangChain, Strands, or Google ADK adapter in Python, the adapter owns the model call. A direct `openai` or `anthropic` call under it adds no second span. In TypeScript this is not complete. See [Known limits](#known-limits).

chunks.heading: LangChain and LangGraph
chunks.text:
| Item                        | Python                                                                                                                                                   | TypeScript                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install                     | `pip install "armoriq-sdk[langchain]"`                                                                                                                   | `@armoriq/sdk` plus `@langchain/core`                                                                          |
| Wire it                     | `ArmorIQLangChain(armoriq_client=..., mode="sdk").for_user(email, goal=...)`, then `config={"callbacks": [handler]}`                                     | `new ArmorIQLangChain({client, mode: 'sdk'}).forUser(email, {goal})`, then `callbacks: [...existing, handler]` |
| Trace ends when             | The root chain ends or fails. A run with only a model call ends when the model call ends or fails.                                                       | The same events                                                                                                |
| Close by hand               | `handler.close(status)` or `await handler.aclose(status)`                                                                                                | `handler.close(status)`                                                                                        |
| Cancel, timeout, disconnect | A cancelled async model-only run ends as `cancelled`. For a timeout or a dropped connection, call `handler.close()` if the framework sends no end event. | The SDK maps an aborted run to `cancelled`, a timeout to `timeout`, and a dropped connection to `disconnected` |
| Callback chaining           | LangChain keeps the callback list. ArmorIQ does not touch the other handlers.                                                                            | You append the handler to your existing list                                                                   |
| Concurrency                 | One handler can serve runs one after another. Two top-level runs at the same time on one handler fail closed. Create one handler for each request.       | One handler can serve many runs. Each root run has its own request state.                                      |
| Native spans                | Detects OpenInference. Not LangSmith.                                                                                                                    | Detects OpenInference in the CommonJS and ES module builds. Not LangSmith.                                     |

Limits for LangChain and LangGraph:

* No LangGraph version is tested. LangGraph passes LangChain callbacks, but ArmorIQ has not run a real LangGraph graph in its tests. Test your exact LangGraph version.
* In Python, the model span is recorded after the model call ends, from the usage that LangChain reports. It is not timed by a start and an end hook.
* In TypeScript, if a model call at the root returns tool calls, the trace stays open until the chain ends or you call `handler.close()`.
* After `handler.close()`, the handler is finished for good. A later tool call on it is blocked. Create a new handler.
* If the framework gives no tool name, ArmorIQ blocks the tool call (fail closed).
* A TypeScript bootstrap failure only logs a warning, and the handler uses a safe fallback for tool names.

chunks.heading: Strands Agents
chunks.text:
| Item            | Python                                                                                                                                                                               | TypeScript                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install         | `pip install "armoriq-sdk[strands]"`                                                                                                                                                 | `@armoriq/sdk` plus `@strands-agents/sdk`                                                                                                    |
| Wire it         | `ArmorIQStrands(armoriq_client=..., mode="sdk").for_user(email, goal=...)`, then `Agent(..., hooks=[hooks])`                                                                         | `new ArmorIQStrands({client, mode: 'sdk'}).forUser(email, {goal})`, then `new Agent({..., plugins: [plugin]})`                               |
| Hooks used      | Before and after invocation, before and after model call, before and after tool call                                                                                                 | After model call, before and after tool call, and (when the framework has them) before model call and after invocation                       |
| Trace ends when | The invocation ends. The status is `error` if there is no result, `cancelled` for a stop reason such as cancelled or interrupted, `denied` after a policy block, and `ok` otherwise. | The invocation ends. The status comes from the cancel signal (timeout, disconnect, or cancelled), then from an error, and is `ok` otherwise. |
| Close by hand   | `hooks.close()`                                                                                                                                                                      | `plugin.close(status)`. It finishes the plugin for good.                                                                                     |
| Concurrency     | Uses the mutable `invocation_state` of Strands for each request. If it is missing, ArmorIQ fails closed.                                                                             | The plugin keys request state by `invocationState`                                                                                           |
| Native spans    | No detection. Strands telemetry is not read.                                                                                                                                         | No detection.                                                                                                                                |

Limits for Strands:

* Register exactly one ArmorIQ hook provider on an agent. A second one raises an error. Your own hooks can stay.
* In Python the ArmorIQ guard wraps the tool run stage of Strands 1.54.x. If that part of Strands changes, ArmorIQ fails closed.
* In TypeScript the event classes must come from the same Strands copy as the agent. If your host gives older classes without the invocation-end event, call `plugin.close()` yourself.
* In TypeScript, without the before-model event, the model span has about 0 ms duration.
* If you pass no `goal`, the root and model input show that the framework gave no goal (`framework_goal_not_provided`).

chunks.heading: Google ADK
chunks.text:
| Item              | Python                                                                                                                  | TypeScript                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Install           | `pip install "armoriq-sdk[google-adk]"`                                                                                 | `@armoriq/sdk` plus `@google/adk`                                                                                                                  |
| Wire it           | `ArmorIQADK(api_key=...).for_user(email, goal=...)`, then `scope.install(root_agent)` and `scope.uninstall(root_agent)` | `new ArmorIQADK({apiKey}).forUser(email, {goal})`, then `bundle.install(agent)`                                                                    |
| Hooks used        | Before and after model callback, before and after tool callback                                                         | The same four callbacks                                                                                                                            |
| Trace ends when   | `uninstall()` runs and closes with status `ok`. To record a failure, call `close("error")` before `uninstall()`.        | The wrapped `runAsync` ends or fails. Success is `ok`. An error gets the status of the error. Leaving the loop early is `cancelled`.               |
| Close by hand     | `close(status)` or `aclose(status)`                                                                                     | `await bundle.close(status)`. A bundle serves one request.                                                                                         |
| Callback chaining | The adapter wraps your four callbacks and calls them with ADK rules. `uninstall()` restores them exactly.               | The adapter puts its callbacks first and keeps yours after them in the same list. If you replace a slot later, ArmorIQ chains behind it and warns. |
| Concurrency       | Uses a context variable for each request. The callback registry is process-wide. A stale context fails closed.          | Installing a second live bundle on the same agent in the same async context raises an error.                                                       |
| Native spans      | No detection.                                                                                                           | No detection. The adapter pairs one model span for each ADK invocation.                                                                            |

Limits for Google ADK:

* The Python `ArmorIQADK` builds its own client. It has no `observability` argument, so set export options with environment variables. See [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership#settings-reference).
* In TypeScript, ADK must supply `functionCallId` for exact tool matching. Without it, the adapter matches tool calls in order and logs one warning for the process. The warning has no tool, user, or argument data.
* In TypeScript, a plan-assurance gate can run after the model call if `papGatewayUrl` is set or `ARMORIQ_PAP_FORCE=1`. It can replace the model response.

chunks.heading: Direct OpenAI and Anthropic calls
chunks.text:
You do not install an adapter for these. The SDK patches the provider packages when you create an `ArmorIQClient`. A call produces one model span, but only while an ArmorIQ session is active.

| Item             | Python                                                                                                                                                                        | TypeScript                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Traced calls     | OpenAI chat completions and responses (`create`, `parse`). Anthropic messages and beta messages (`create`).                                                                   | OpenAI chat completions and responses (`create`). Anthropic messages and beta messages (`create`). This includes streaming calls and `messages.stream()`.                         |
| Streaming        | **Not traced.** A call with `stream=True` produces no span.                                                                                                                   | Traced. The span ends when the stream finishes, fails, or is closed early. A stream that you stop before it finishes is `cancelled`.                                              |
| Data captured    | Model name and provider, input and output tokens, cache tokens, and status. The prompt and completion are captured only when the capture mode and organization allow content. | The same                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Manual call      | `instrument_openai()`, `instrument_anthropic()`                                                                                                                               | `instrumentOpenAI(OpenAI)`, `instrumentAnthropic(Anthropic)`. An ES module app must call `instrumentOpenAI(OpenAI)` itself, because the automatic patch loads the CommonJS build. |
| Which session    | The session bound to the current context, or the only open session. With several open sessions and none bound, the call produces no span.                                     | The session bound to the current async flow                                                                                                                                       |
| Under an adapter | One span only. The adapter owns the model call.                                                                                                                               | **Can produce a second span.** See below.                                                                                                                                         |

In Python, a model call produces no direct span when any of these is true: the call streams, no session is bound, a framework adapter owns the call, or the call is already inside another direct span. An OpenAI call that times out ends as `timeout`. A cancelled call ends as `cancelled`.

In TypeScript, an OpenAI streaming chat request gets `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` by default so that token counts arrive. Set `ARMORIQ_OTEL_STREAM_USAGE=0` (or `observability.streamUsage: false`) if your gateway rejects it. An explicit `stream_options` on your request is never changed.

chunks.heading: CrewAI
chunks.text: CrewAI tracing is **not supported yet**. The Python `ArmorIQCrew` class still does intent verification and enforcement for CrewAI tools. It creates no session, no spans, and no trace. Do not expect model, policy, tool, or end-of-run spans from a CrewAI run. Zero-touch CrewAI tracing is planned work, tracked in armoriq-sdk-customer issue 124.

chunks.heading: Known limits
chunks.text:
* **Python and TypeScript differ for direct calls under an adapter.** In TypeScript, a raw `openai` or `anthropic` call made under a LangChain, Strands, or Google ADK adapter produces its own `gen_ai.chat` span in addition to the adapter's span. Python avoids the second span. This TypeScript gap is tracked in armoriq-sdk-customer-ts issue 287.
* **Spans that start before the first policy answer.** The SDK reads your organization policy before it records data. The TypeScript SDK does not wait for it with the `armoriq` and `provider` exports, so spans that start before the first answer are not recorded. The Python SDK waits for the first answer, for up to 5 seconds. See [Troubleshooting](/platform/observability/troubleshooting#the-first-spans-of-a-new-process-are-missing).
* **A run that never ends.** The SDK exports only spans that have ended. If a framework never sends an end event and you do not close the session, the root span is not exported.
* **Process exit.** A TypeScript process that exits normally drains ended spans, up to a fixed time, and stops after three idle rounds. The SDK does not handle `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, or `process.exit()`. Close sessions before your process stops.
* **TypeScript adapter imports.** The adapters are not exported from the package root. Import them from `@armoriq/sdk/dist/integrations/<name>`.
