chunks.heading: Observability Overview
chunks.text:
ArmorIQ Observability shows what an agent did, why an action was allowed or denied, how long each operation took, and how many model tokens it used. Use it to investigate a single run or to watch activity across an organization.

The SDKs record each agent run as an OpenTelemetry trace. OpenTelemetry is an open standard for trace data. You add no tracing code. Your administrators decide how much data ArmorIQ keeps.

chunks.heading: Who this is for
chunks.text:
Observability is for agent developers who debug runs, integration owners who check SDK and product telemetry, security teams who review policy outcomes and data capture, and operators who watch reliability, latency, and usage across an organization.

<Callout type="info">
  Observability is telemetry, not an enforcement dependency. A telemetry error does not change a policy decision or fail the agent operation. Ending a session waits a short, fixed time to send the last spans, so a destination that is not reachable can add that wait at the end of a run.
</Callout>

chunks.heading: How telemetry moves
chunks.text: 1. The SDK reads your organization capture policy. It records only what the policy allows. 2. The SDK builds spans for plans, policy decisions, model calls, and tool work, and exports them. By default they go to ArmorIQ over **OTLP**, the standard OpenTelemetry way to send traces over HTTP. 3. ArmorIQ checks your API key, applies the organization policy again, removes secrets, and stores the spans. 4. The dashboard reads the stored data for the organization that you select. You can also send traces to your own destination, with or instead of ArmorIQ. See [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership) and [Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector](/platform/observability/collector).

chunks.heading: Session, trace, and span
Where to go next
chunks.text:
| I want to...                                               | Read                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Turn on tracing for an agent                               | [Set up tracing](/platform/observability/quickstart)                         |
| Know which frameworks work and which versions are tested   | [Framework support](/platform/observability/frameworks)                      |
| Send traces to my own tool, or use my own tracer provider  | [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership) |
| Run a Collector with batching, retry, and TLS              | [Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector](/platform/observability/collector)       |
| Know what data is stored and what is never stored          | [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture)                |
| Set capture mode, scopes, debug capture, quota, and alerts | [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls)       |
| Move from an older SDK                                     | [Migrate from the legacy recorder](/platform/observability/migration)        |
| Fix a missing or incomplete trace                          | [Troubleshooting](/platform/observability/troubleshooting)                   |

chunks.heading: Supported producers
chunks.text:
| Producer                                                        | How it records telemetry                                                                                              | When data normally becomes visible                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [TypeScript SDK](/platform/observability/typescript-sdk) 0.8.23 | OpenTelemetry spans, exported in batches over OTLP                                                                    | After the spans end and are sent. The last spans send when the session closes. |
| [Python SDK](/platform/observability/python-sdk) 0.8.17         | OpenTelemetry spans, exported in batches over OTLP                                                                    | After the spans end and are sent. The last spans send when the session closes. |
| ArmorCodex and ArmorClaude                                      | Per-turn bridges. Builds that use the current SDK send over OTLP. Builds that use an older SDK send to the old route. | After the turn ends and the bridge sends it                                    |
| Any OTLP source                                                 | A Collector or another sender that follows [the ingest rules](/platform/observability/collector#what-armoriq-accepts) | After ArmorIQ accepts the request                                              |

See [ArmorCodex and ArmorClaude](/platform/observability/armorcodex-armorclaude) for the product-specific lifecycle.

chunks.heading: What is captured
chunks.text:
By default ArmorIQ keeps metadata: the shape of the run, policy decisions, status, timing, token counts, cost, and safe error types. Prompts, completions, and tool inputs and outputs are kept only when your organization chooses the Enhanced or Debug capture mode **and** allows content capture. Secrets and personal identifiers are always removed. Read [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture) for the full table.

Not every producer supplies every field. A value can show as `--` or **Not reported** in the dashboard. See [Missing values and zero values](/platform/observability/dashboard#missing-values-and-zero-values).

chunks.heading: Freshness and retention
chunks.text:
* The SDK sends spans in batches, and sends the rest when the session closes.
* The dashboard polls every 30 seconds. It does not use WebSocket or server-sent event streaming.
* ArmorCodex and ArmorClaude normally complete a trace at the end of a turn, so data can appear after the turn finishes.
* The backend retains observability traces and sessions for 30 days by default. Operators can change the server-side retention period with `OBSERVABILITY_RETENTION_DAYS`.

chunks.heading: Failure and privacy boundaries
chunks.text:
Sending is best-effort. An SDK retries a failed send a few times, then drops the batch and logs a warning. It does not raise into the agent workflow, and it never switches to another path. Policy decisions stay independent from telemetry success.

The SDK and the ArmorIQ backend both remove secrets and personal identifiers from every mode. Redaction uses patterns, so it cannot find every secret. Do not put secrets in prompts or tool arguments, and limit dashboard access to the people who need it. If you export spans to another tool, ArmorIQ cannot take them back. See [What the Off setting does and does not do](/platform/observability/organization-controls#what-the-off-setting-does-and-does-not-do).

chunks.heading: Migrate From the Legacy Recorder
chunks.text: This guide is for developers and operators who run an ArmorIQ SDK that still uses the legacy recorder (`ObservabilityRecorder`). You get the list of removed APIs, the steps to move to OpenTelemetry, and a clear rule about what the SDK will and will not do if something fails.

chunks.heading: Migration support and runtime fallback are different things
chunks.text:
These two ideas are easy to confuse.

|                  | Migration support                                                                                                                      | Runtime fallback                                                     |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| What it is       | The ArmorIQ backend keeps an old route open for a limited time, so an older client that you have not upgraded yet still delivers data. | The SDK changes to another path on its own when the main path fails. |
| Who does it      | The backend                                                                                                                            | The SDK                                                              |
| Does it exist?   | **Yes, for a limited time.**                                                                                                           | **No.** The current SDKs have none.                                  |
| Which route      | `POST /observability/spans` (old JSON route)                                                                                           | Not applicable                                                       |
| Is it permanent? | No. ArmorIQ plans to remove the old route after all clients have migrated.                                                             | Not applicable                                                       |

**Migration support.** The backend still accepts `POST /observability/spans` from older SDK clients. This gives you time to upgrade. Do not build anything new on that route. ArmorIQ plans to remove it after all consumers move to the current SDK, and it will not bring it back as a rollback path. Old traces that are already stored stay readable.

**No runtime fallback.** The current SDK sends traces one way only: OTLP to `POST /v1/traces`, or to the OTLP endpoint or provider that you choose. It never sends to the old route. The SDK has no `pipeline` setting and no mixed mode. If a destination is missing, rejected, or not reachable, the SDK exports nothing and the agent continues. It does not pick another destination, another transport, or local storage. A test in each SDK checks that the production code contains no reference to the old route.

chunks.heading: What changed
chunks.text:
<Callout type="warn">
  The current releases (Python 0.8.17, TypeScript 0.8.23) break compatibility with the legacy recorder. If your version range does not include them, change it when you are ready to move.
</Callout>

| Removed                                                                                                                                                                                | Use instead                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The in-memory recorder and shipper: `ObservabilityRecorder`, `ObservabilityShipper`, and the recorder handle functions (the functions that started and ended traces and spans by hand) | The SDK builds an OpenTelemetry span tree for each session by itself. You call nothing.                                                                                                        |
| `ObservabilityConfig` (Python) and `defaultObservabilityConfig` and `ObservabilityConfig` (TypeScript)                                                                                 | `ObservabilityOptions` on the client, and the per-session switch below                                                                                                                         |
| Python: `ShipperConfig`, `TraceSummary`, the JSON schemas, and the session members `observability_recorder` and `active_plan_trace_context`                                            | Nothing. The SDK handles these inside the session.                                                                                                                                             |
| TypeScript: the schema and trace-summary exports, and `ArmorIQSession.observabilityRecorder` and `ArmorIQSession.activePlanTraceContext`                                               | `session.otelSession`                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ObservabilityOptions.pipeline`, the pipeline mode type, and `ARMORIQ_OTEL_PIPELINE`                                                                                                   | Nothing. OpenTelemetry is the only path.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ObservabilityConfig.enabled` (Python)                                                                                                                                                 | `SessionOptions(observability_enabled=False)`                                                                                                                                                  |
| The old environment variables `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT` and `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY_PRODUCT`                                                                                     | The SDK no longer reads them. ArmorIQ takes your organization and product from your API key. To send elsewhere, use `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORTER` and the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables. |
| The Python model price table: `MODEL_PRICES`, `ModelPrice`, and `compute_cost_usd`                                                                                                     | ArmorIQ prices model usage when it receives a span. Pass `cost_usd` only when your provider reports a cost.                                                                                    |
| `POST /observability/spans`                                                                                                                                                            | `POST /v1/traces`                                                                                                                                                                              |

Two things look different in the dashboard after you move. The SDK now makes one trace for each session. Its root span is `armoriq.agent.run`, and its plan is a child span named `armoriq.intent.plan`. Trace IDs are standard OpenTelemetry IDs, which have 32 hexadecimal characters.

chunks.heading: Move your agent
chunks.text:
1. **Upgrade the SDK.** For Python install `armoriq-sdk==0.8.17`. For TypeScript install `@armoriq/sdk@0.8.23`. Change any version range that excludes these versions.
2. **Delete recorder code.** Remove every use of the recorder, the shipper, the handle functions, and the trace summary. Remove manual start, end, and flush calls for traces and spans. If you call `session.record_generation(...)` in Python, you can keep it. It now adds a model span.
3. **Move your settings.**
   * To turn tracing off for one session in Python, use `SessionOptions(observability_enabled=False)`.
   * To turn tracing off for one session in TypeScript, use `startSession({ observability: { enabled: false } })`.
   * To send traces to your own endpoint, use the settings in [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership).
4. **Keep your session close.** The close that ends your session also ends the trace. Framework adapters do it for you. See [Set up tracing](/platform/observability/quickstart).
5. **Check the first trace.** Run the agent once. Open **Observability** and confirm that the trace has your policy and tool spans. Read [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture) so that you know what is stored in your organization capture mode.
6. **Check your own tooling.** If a script reads traces from the API, read the [API reference](/platform/observability/api-reference). Spans now have OpenTelemetry names such as `gen_ai.chat` and `armoriq.tool`. Group operations by the `armoriq.operation.category` attribute, not by span name. See the [data model](/platform/observability/data-model).

chunks.heading: What does not change
chunks.text:
* Policy decisions and enforcement. They never depend on telemetry.
* Your API key and organization. ArmorIQ reads both from the key.
* Old traces. They stay in ArmorIQ and stay readable.
* The fail-open rule. A tracing error never changes the result of your agent.

chunks.heading: ArmorClaude and ArmorCodex
chunks.text: ArmorClaude and ArmorCodex builds that bundle an older SDK still send each turn to the old route. Builds that bundle the current SDK send over OTLP. Check which SDK your plugin build uses. See [ArmorCodex and ArmorClaude](/platform/observability/armorcodex-armorclaude).

chunks.heading: Roll back
chunks.text:
The safe way to roll back is to turn tracing off. Set `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY=off`, or use the per-session switch above. Policy enforcement keeps working. Your organization can also set the capture mode to `off` in **Settings > Observability**. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls).

You can also keep your older SDK for now. That works only while the backend still accepts the old route, so treat it as a short-term step. The SDK will not fall back to the old route for you.

chunks.heading: Organization Controls
chunks.text:
This page is for organization administrators and security teams. You learn what you can control on the observability settings page, what each control changes, who is allowed to change it, and what the **Off** setting does not do.

Open **Settings > Observability** in the dashboard. The page is `/dashboard/settings/observability`, and its title is **Observability data collection**. The settings apply to every API key and SDK session in the active organization.

chunks.heading: Capture mode
chunks.text:
The **Data collection** card sets the capture mode. Save it with **Save capture setting**.

| Mode                   | What the page says it does                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Off                    | Stops new observability collection.                                                           |
| Metadata (recommended) | Captures topology, policy decisions, status, latency, token use, cost, and safe error types.  |
| Enhanced               | Captures only organization-approved, redacted and bounded input and output summaries.         |
| Debug                  | Temporary detailed capture. It still uses redaction and bounds, and must end within 24 hours. |

The page also states: "Secrets and credentials are always removed at every capture mode. This cannot be turned off." For the full list of fields, see [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture).

An organization that has never saved a policy uses `metadata`, with content capture off and external content capture off.

chunks.heading: Content capture
chunks.text:
When you choose Enhanced or Debug, two check boxes appear:

1. **Enable redacted content capture for this organization.** You must turn this on to save Enhanced or Debug. It permits bounded, redacted summaries only. It does not permit secrets, credentials, or authentication headers.
2. **Allow redacted content to be sent to an external observability provider.** This lets an SDK that exports to your own destination include redacted content. It needs a separate permission. The page warns that third-party providers have their own access controls, and ArmorIQ membership controls do not apply after export.

chunks.heading: Debug capture
chunks.text:
Debug is a time-limited lease.

* You set **Debug capture ends** to a future time that is no more than 24 hours from now.
* You cannot make an active debug window longer. While it is active, the other modes are locked.
* When the time ends, the effective mode returns to `metadata`.
* Starting or ending debug needs its own permission. Without it, the Debug choice is locked and shows "Needs the debug permission".
* ArmorIQ records the start and the end of debug in the change history.

chunks.heading: When two people save at once
chunks.text: Every save sends the policy revision that you loaded. If someone else saved first, ArmorIQ rejects your save. The page shows "Someone else changed this policy. The latest version is loaded; review and save again." Review the new values and save again.

chunks.heading: Scope overrides
chunks.text:
The **Effective policy** section shows what each scope collects after the organization setting is applied. Its columns are Scope, ID, Set mode, Effective mode, and Note. The first row is the organization.

You can add a scope override for one **product**. The **Scope overrides** card lists the products, and you pick a capture mode for the one you choose.

* A scope can only **lower** collection. A scope can never collect more than the organization allows. A mode above the organization mode is locked.
* A scope cannot turn on collection that the organization turned off.
* A local SDK setting follows the same rule. It can only lower collection.
* **Only product scopes are available today.** The API key identifies only the organization and the product, so ArmorIQ cannot yet tell which environment or agent sent a span. New environment and agent scopes are refused. Older environment or agent rows still show, marked **Not enforced yet**. They do not change what ArmorIQ collects, and you can remove them.
* **Remove** a scope to return collection for that scope to the organization mode. ArmorIQ asks you to confirm.

chunks.heading: Usage and pipeline health
chunks.text: The **Usage and pipeline health** card shows how much your organization uses and whether telemetry arrives. You can filter by product.

chunks.heading: Monthly quota
chunks.text:
Two cards show **Spans** and **Storage** as "used of limit" for the current month (a calendar month in UTC). Used counts both committed and reserved capacity.

| Badge                                 | Meaning                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Approaching limit                     | Use is at 80 percent of the limit, or more |
| Limit reached                         | New telemetry is rejected                  |
| Quota is 0, new telemetry is rejected | The limit is set to zero                   |

When a quota is full, ArmorIQ answers an SDK or Collector with `429` and `Retry-After: 60`. A retry is safe.

chunks.heading: Ingest pipeline
chunks.text:
The pipeline status looks at the last 24 hours.

| Status                       | When it appears                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Healthy                      | Telemetry arrives and nothing is rejected or slow                     |
| Delayed                      | The slowest ingest request took more than 30 seconds                  |
| Rejecting                    | Any span was rejected, any request failed, or any span failed mapping |
| Unavailable                  | Ingest is switched off by an operator                                 |
| Status unknown               | The page could not load the data                                      |
| No telemetry in the last 24h | No requests arrived                                                   |

The counters are: accepted spans, rejected spans, duplicate spans, mapping-failure spans, failed requests, average ingest handling time, and maximum ingest handling time. The page notes that dropped telemetry is the sum of rejected spans and mapping-failure spans.

For help with a bad status, see [Troubleshooting](/platform/observability/troubleshooting#check-the-health-signals).

chunks.heading: Change history
Alert rules
chunks.text:
**Alert rules** check your telemetry on a schedule. A rule opens a **firing** when its condition is met, and resolves it when the condition clears. ArmorIQ checks the rules every 5 minutes. Open **Recent firings** on a rule to see its history. Each rule has a severity of Info, Warning, or Critical.

| Condition                      | What it measures over the window                                              | Unit         |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| Policy denial rate             | Share of policy decisions that deny or block                                  | Percent      |
| Tool error rate                | Share of tool, command, and MCP spans that end in error                       | Percent      |
| Model error rate               | Share of model spans that end in error                                        | Percent      |
| p95 latency                    | The 95th percentile duration of tool, command, MCP, and model spans           | Milliseconds |
| Token cost                     | Total model cost over whole UTC hours                                         | USD          |
| Token count                    | Total tokens over whole UTC hours                                             | Tokens       |
| Retry rate                     | Share of operations that were retried                                         | Percent      |
| Timeout rate                   | Share of operations that timed out                                            | Percent      |
| Exporter ingest rejection rate | The higher of the span rejection rate and the failed request rate             | Percent      |
| Missing telemetry              | Any product that sent data before now sends fewer requests than the threshold | Requests     |

The window is 1 to 1,440 minutes. For the two budget rules, the window is 60 to 1,440 minutes. A percent threshold is at most 100, and the missing-telemetry threshold is at least 1. You turn a rule off with **Disable**. The rule stays in the list, and you can enable it again. You need the alert manage permission to change a rule.

chunks.heading: Delete data and export
chunks.text:
**Delete data** permanently removes specific traces and their spans from ArmorIQ. You enter trace IDs (UUID version 4), then confirm by typing `DELETE`. Deletion is blocked while a legal hold is active. An export that includes a deleted trace is invalidated. Deletion removes data from ArmorIQ only. It does not remove copies that you exported to another system.

**Export traces** is on the Observability overview page, not on the settings page. It starts an encrypted export of your most recent traces (1 to 100) as a `.jsonl` file. At most two exports can run for an organization at the same time.

chunks.heading: Permissions
chunks.text:
Each control has its own permission. The dashboard hides or locks a control when you lack the permission.

| What you want to do                                        | Permission needed                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| See metadata, effective policy, usage, and pipeline health | Observability metadata read                   |
| See captured content in a trace                            | Observability content read                    |
| Change the capture mode and scope overrides                | Observability settings manage (full)          |
| See change history                                         | Observability settings (view or full)         |
| Start, change, or end debug capture                        | Observability debug manage                    |
| Allow content to go to an external provider                | Observability external export manage          |
| See alert rules                                            | Observability alert read                      |
| Create, change, enable, or disable alert rules             | Observability alert manage                    |
| Export traces                                              | Observability export create, and content read |
| Delete traces                                              | Observability delete execute                  |
| Manage a legal hold                                        | Observability legal hold manage               |

By default, the organization admin role has every one of these permissions. Other default roles have fewer. For example, one default role can start debug capture but cannot change the settings. A person without the content read permission sees a "Permission required" page when they open a trace. They still see metadata in the trace and session lists.

chunks.heading: What the Off setting does and does not do
chunks.text:
Setting the capture mode to **Off** controls **ArmorIQ collection only**. It does not remove data that has already left, and it cannot take back a third-party export.

**Off does this:**

* ArmorIQ stores no new telemetry for your organization. If a request arrives, ArmorIQ answers with success and writes nothing.
* SDKs read the organization policy. While it says Off, they create no ArmorIQ spans, for every export choice. This starts when the SDK next reads its policy. The SDK reads the policy again at least every 5 minutes, and sooner when a policy check from ArmorIQ tells it that the policy changed. For an SDK-owned pipeline, the SDK also checks the policy again just before spans leave the process, so spans that are still in the queue do not ship.
* Policy enforcement keeps running. A decision to allow, hold, or block does not change.

**Off does not do this:**

* **It cannot revoke a third-party export.** After a span goes to your Collector, your own provider, or another tool, ArmorIQ cannot take it back. That destination has its own access rules. ArmorIQ membership controls do not apply there. This is also true if you later turn off external content capture. The new setting stops future exports only.
* **It does not control tracing that is not from ArmorIQ.** Spans that your application or another tool creates, such as OpenInference spans or your own OpenTelemetry code, are not ArmorIQ spans. ArmorIQ does not change, flush, or stop your provider. It only stops its own spans.
* **It does not delete stored data.** Use **Delete data** for that.
* **It does not turn off policy enforcement.** The page says this when an operator switch is off: "Turning a telemetry switch off does not turn policy enforcement off. Organization and scope limits still apply."

If you must be sure that no ArmorIQ data reaches a destination, remove the `external` or `provider` export in your code or Collector, and keep the capture mode at Off.

chunks.heading: Operator switches (self-hosted backends)
chunks.text:
Operators of an ArmorIQ backend can switch parts of observability off with environment variables. All of them are on by default. A switch accepts only `true` or `false`. Any other value stops the backend at start-up, so a typo cannot change collection. A switch can only lower collection. It never turns on a mode and never skips redaction.

| Variable                                 | When set to `false`                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OBSERVABILITY_OTLP_INGEST_ENABLED`      | The OTLP route still checks the request, but it stores nothing and returns success. The effective mode shows as Off. |
| `OBSERVABILITY_ENHANCED_CONTENT_ENABLED` | Enhanced capture is lowered to `metadata`.                                                                           |
| `OBSERVABILITY_DEBUG_CAPTURE_ENABLED`    | Debug capture is lowered to `metadata`.                                                                              |
| `OBSERVABILITY_LEASE_DELIVERY_ENABLED`   | The SDK policy route answers `503`.                                                                                  |
| `OBSERVABILITY_DASHBOARD_READS_ENABLED`  | The organization observability routes answer `503`. This includes the routes that change settings.                   |

Two more variables help with recovery:

* `OTEL_CANONICAL_WRITER_ENABLED=false` stops the backend from writing new telemetry. Spans are reported as rejected. Stored data is not deleted or changed, and no other path takes over.
* `OBSERVABILITY_INGEST_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_MS` sets the ingest write time limit (default 10,000 ms, kept between 1,000 and 30,000).

chunks.heading: Choose Who Exports Your Traces
chunks.text: This page is for developers and platform engineers who already run OpenTelemetry, or who want to send ArmorIQ traces to another tool. You learn the three export choices, who owns the tracer provider in each one, and how to configure them.

chunks.heading: Terms used on this page
chunks.text:
* A **span** is one timed step in an agent run, for example one tool call. A **trace** is all the spans of one run.
* A **TracerProvider** is the OpenTelemetry object that creates spans and passes them to an exporter.
* An **exporter** sends finished spans to a destination.
* **OTLP** (OpenTelemetry Protocol) is the standard format and HTTP route that OpenTelemetry tools use to exchange traces. The SDK sends OTLP over HTTP with protobuf encoding (`http/protobuf`). It supports no other OTLP encoding.
* An **OpenTelemetry Collector** is a service that you run. It receives spans, processes them, and forwards them to one or more destinations. See [Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector](/platform/observability/collector).

chunks.heading: The three choices
chunks.text:
One SDK runtime has exactly one export choice. You set it with the `exporter` option.

| `exporter`          | Who owns the TracerProvider                 | Where spans go                                               | Data limit                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `armoriq` (default) | ArmorIQ (a private provider inside the SDK) | `POST /v1/traces` on your ArmorIQ backend, with your API key | The organization capture policy                                                                                       |
| `external`          | ArmorIQ (a private provider inside the SDK) | The OTLP endpoint that you set, for example a Collector      | The organization capture policy. Prompt and tool content leave only if the organization also allows external content. |
| `provider`          | Your application                            | Wherever your own provider sends them                        | **Metadata only**, always                                                                                             |

If you set an unknown value in the `exporter` option, the SDK uses `armoriq`.

chunks.heading: ArmorIQ-owned provider
chunks.text:
With `armoriq` and `external`, the SDK builds a private tracer provider with its own batch exporter. The provider stays isolated from your application:

* The SDK never registers its provider as the global OpenTelemetry provider.
* The SDK never changes, replaces, or shuts down a provider that your application created.
* In TypeScript, ArmorIQ spans start from an empty trace context. The trace context of your own web request does not leak into the ArmorIQ trace.
* When the session or client closes, the SDK flushes its own provider, and shuts it down when the last user of that provider closes. A close is bounded in time. It never blocks your agent for long.

Use these choices when you want ArmorIQ to manage export and keep your own OpenTelemetry setup unchanged.

chunks.heading: Application-owned provider
chunks.text:
With `provider`, you pass your own tracer provider. The SDK only asks it for a tracer named `armoriq_sdk`. Then:

* The SDK adds no span processor and no exporter to your provider.
* The SDK never flushes, shuts down, or changes your provider. You control destination, sampling, and batching.
* ArmorIQ capture is limited to `metadata`. The SDK cannot re-check the organization policy on spans that wait in a queue that it does not own. So it never records prompts, completions, tool arguments, or tool results in this mode. To capture content, use `armoriq` or `external`.
* In TypeScript, the root span of a session becomes a child of the active span in your application.

<Callout type="info">
  Provider mode needs a provider. If you set `exporter` to `provider` and give no provider, the SDK exports nothing. See [Troubleshooting](/platform/observability/troubleshooting#no-provider-mode).
</Callout>

chunks.heading: Configure the export
chunks.text:
<Tabs groupId="language" items="['Python', 'TypeScript']">
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    from armoriq_sdk import ArmorIQClient, ObservabilityOptions

    # 1. ArmorIQ OTLP (default). No options needed.
    client = ArmorIQClient(api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"])

    # 2. Your own OTLP endpoint, for example a Collector.
    client = ArmorIQClient(
        api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"],
        observability=ObservabilityOptions(
            exporter="external",
            endpoint="https://collector.example.com/v1/traces",
            headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['COLLECTOR_TOKEN']}"},
        ),
    )

    # 3. Your own tracer provider.
    client = ArmorIQClient(
        api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"],
        observability=ObservabilityOptions(
            exporter="provider",
            tracer_provider=my_tracer_provider,
        ),
    )
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { ArmorIQClient } from '@armoriq/sdk';

    // 1. ArmorIQ OTLP (default). No options needed.
    const client = new ArmorIQClient({ apiKey: process.env.ARMORIQ_API_KEY! });

    // 2. Your own OTLP endpoint, for example a Collector.
    const external = new ArmorIQClient({
      apiKey: process.env.ARMORIQ_API_KEY!,
      observability: {
        exporter: 'external',
        endpoint: 'https://collector.example.com/v1/traces',
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.COLLECTOR_TOKEN}` },
      },
    });

    // 3. Your own tracer provider.
    const session = client.startSession({
      observability: { exporter: 'provider', tracerProvider: myTracerProvider },
    });
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can use the standard OpenTelemetry environment variables instead of code. Keep tokens in a secret store and inject them as environment variables. Do not write them in source files.

```bash
export ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORTER=external
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=https://collector.example.com/v1/traces
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS="authorization=Bearer%20${COLLECTOR_TOKEN}"
```

Header values use URL encoding, so a space is `%20`. Do not set a `content-type` header. The SDK always sends `application/x-protobuf`.

chunks.heading: Rules for the endpoint
chunks.text:
* Use `https:` for any host that is not on your own machine. The SDK accepts `http:` only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1`. A plain `http:` request would send your headers and permitted content in clear text.
* Do not put a user name, password, query string, or fragment in the URL.
* The SDK uses the first endpoint setting that it finds. It does not try the next one when the first is invalid. If that setting is not valid, the SDK exports nothing.
* If you set no endpoint, the SDK exports nothing. It does **not** fall back to `localhost`. It does **not** fall back to ArmorIQ.
* After an export fails, the SDK does not switch to another destination.

chunks.heading: Settings reference
chunks.text:
| Setting                                | Python                                                                                                                                                                                         | TypeScript                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pick the exporter                      | `ObservabilityOptions(exporter=...)`. The variable `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORTER` overrides the option.                                                                                               | `observability.exporter`. The option wins over `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORTER`. If you set neither and an endpoint setting exists, the SDK chooses `external`.                         |
| Endpoint order (first one set is used) | `endpoint` option, `ARMORIQ_OTEL_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, then `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`                                                                           | `endpoint` option, `baseEndpoint` option, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, then `ARMORIQ_OTEL_ENDPOINT`                                    |
| Base endpoint form                     | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. The SDK adds `/v1/traces`.                                                                                                                                      | `baseEndpoint` option or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. The SDK adds `/v1/traces`.                                                                                             |
| Headers                                | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, then `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS`, then the `headers` option. Later items win.                                                                            | Same order                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Timeout                                | `timeout_millis`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT`, `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Default 10 seconds. The SDK keeps the value between 0.1 and 30 seconds. | `timeoutMillis`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT`. Default 10 seconds. A value that is not a positive whole number turns external export off. |
| Custom CA and client certificate       | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_KEY` (and the `_TRACES_` forms). `external` only.                                        | Not supported. Terminate TLS settings in a Collector.                                                                                                                          |
| Service name                           | `service_name` option or `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`. The client uses `agent_id` when you set neither.                                                                                                 | `serviceName` option or `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`. The default is `armoriq-sdk`.                                                                                                     |
| Local data ceiling                     | `capture_mode` option or `ARMORIQ_OTEL_CAPTURE_MODE`. The variable overrides the option.                                                                                                       | `captureMode` option or `ARMORIQ_OTEL_CAPTURE_MODE`. The option wins.                                                                                                          |
| Turn tracing off                       | `observability_enabled=False` on the session, `ObservabilityOptions(enabled=False)`, or `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY`                                                                                | `observability.enabled = false`, `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY`, `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true`, or `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none`                                                             |

The TypeScript SDK does not support gRPC, OTLP/JSON, request compression, HTTP proxy settings, or mTLS in its own exporter. If you need one of these, send to a Collector and set it there.

chunks.heading: What every export choice still obeys
chunks.text:
* **The organization policy is the upper limit.** The SDK reads your organization capture policy with your API key. A local setting can only lower the data that you capture. It can never raise it. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls).
* **External export waits for the policy.** With `external`, the TypeScript SDK waits up to 1.4 seconds for the policy before the first trace of a session. If the policy does not arrive in time, external export stays off for that session. The agent runs as normal.
* **Failures never change the agent result.** A slow or broken destination can drop spans. It never changes what your agent returns.
* **No API key leaves ArmorIQ.** The `external` choice sends only the headers that you configure. It does not send your ArmorIQ API key to the destination.

chunks.heading: Which choice should I use?
chunks.text:
* Use `armoriq` if you only need ArmorIQ dashboards. This is the default.
* Use `external` with a Collector if you want to send traces to ArmorIQ **and** to another tool. The Collector can send the same spans to both. See [Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector](/platform/observability/collector).
* Use `provider` only if your application must own the export pipeline. You accept the metadata-only limit.

chunks.heading: Python SDK Observability
chunks.text:
This page is for Python developers. You learn how tracing works in the `armoriq-sdk` package, which options and environment variables control it, and which session calls are optional. The SDK builds one OpenTelemetry trace for each session, and sends it to ArmorIQ without telemetry code in your agent.

<Callout type="warn">
  This page describes `armoriq-sdk` **0.8.17**, the current release. Older versions used a different recorder. See [Migrate from the legacy recorder](/platform/observability/migration).
</Callout>

chunks.heading: Install
chunks.text:
You need an organization-scoped [ArmorIQ API key](/platform/api-keys/create-key). The SDK supports Python 3.10 to 3.13.

```bash
python -m pip install "armoriq-sdk==0.8.17"
```

Install an extra for the framework that you use: `armoriq-sdk[langchain]`, `armoriq-sdk[strands]`, or `armoriq-sdk[google-adk]`. The import package is `armoriq_sdk`. The OpenTelemetry packages that the SDK needs (`opentelemetry-*`, version 1.27 up to, but not including, 2) install with it.

chunks.heading: Default setup
chunks.text:
Tracing is on by default. With a framework adapter you add no tracing code. See [Set up tracing](/platform/observability/quickstart) for a complete example and [Framework support](/platform/observability/frameworks) for tested versions.

```python
import os
from armoriq_sdk import ArmorIQClient
from armoriq_sdk.integrations.langchain import ArmorIQLangChain

armoriq = ArmorIQLangChain(
    armoriq_client=ArmorIQClient(api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"]),
    mode="sdk",
)
handler = armoriq.for_user("alice@example.com", goal=user_message)
agent_executor.invoke({"input": user_message}, config={"callbacks": [handler]})
```

Creating an `ArmorIQClient` also patches the `openai` and `anthropic` packages, so that direct calls are traced while a session is active.

chunks.heading: Use a session without an adapter
chunks.text:
If you call the session API yourself, the session is also the trace. Use it as a context manager. When the block ends, the SDK ends the trace and sends the spans.

```python
from armoriq_sdk import ArmorIQClient, ReportOptions, SessionOptions

client = ArmorIQClient(api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"], agent_id="crm-assistant")

tool_name = "crm-mcp__search_contacts"
tool_input = {"query": "Acme"}

with client.start_session(SessionOptions(mode="sdk")) as session:
    session.start_plan(
        [{"name": tool_name, "args": tool_input}],
        goal="Find contacts at Acme",
    )
    decision = session.check(tool_name, tool_input)
    if decision.allowed:
        result = run_the_tool(tool_name, tool_input)
        session.report(tool_name, tool_input, result, ReportOptions(status="success"))
```

* `start_plan()`, `check()`, and `report()` add the plan, policy, and tool spans for you.
* If the block raises, the trace ends with status `error`. Otherwise it ends with `ok`.
* Close the session before you close the client.
* You can call `session.close()` or `session.dispose()` instead of the `with` block. Both are safe to call more than once and never raise.

chunks.heading: Optional session calls
chunks.text:
| Call                                                                        | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `session.record_generation(model=..., input_tokens=..., output_tokens=...)` | Adds one model span from usage that you report. Optional arguments are `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `prompt`, `completion`, `finish_reason`, `duration_ms`, and `cost_usd`. Pass `cost_usd` only when your provider reported a cost. Framework adapters do this for you. |
| `session.flush_observability()`                                             | Ends the current plan span and sends queued spans. The session stays open, so you can start another plan. Most agents do not need it.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SessionOptions(observability_enabled=False)`                               | Turns tracing off for this session only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

None of these calls changes a policy decision. They never raise into your code.

chunks.heading: Options
chunks.text:
Pass `ObservabilityOptions` to `ArmorIQClient(observability=...)`.

```python
from armoriq_sdk import ArmorIQClient, ObservabilityOptions

client = ArmorIQClient(
    api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"],
    observability=ObservabilityOptions(capture_mode="metadata"),
)
```

| Field             | Default               | Effect                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`         | `True`                | Turns tracing off for the client when `False`                                                                                 |
| `exporter`        | `"armoriq"`           | `"armoriq"`, `"external"`, or `"provider"`. See [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership). |
| `endpoint`        | none                  | The full OTLP traces URL for `external` export                                                                                |
| `tracer_provider` | none                  | Your OpenTelemetry tracer provider, for `provider` export                                                                     |
| `capture_mode`    | none (no local limit) | The most data that you allow locally: `off`, `metadata`, `enhanced`, or `debug`. The organization policy can lower it more.   |
| `service_name`    | The client `agent_id` | The OpenTelemetry `service.name` of an SDK-owned provider                                                                     |
| `headers`         | none                  | Extra headers for `external` export                                                                                           |
| `protocol`        | `http/protobuf`       | The only supported value                                                                                                      |
| `timeout_millis`  | 10,000                | Export time limit. The SDK keeps it between 100 and 30,000.                                                                   |

A local `capture_mode` can only lower what the organization allows. It can never raise it. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls).

chunks.heading: Environment variables
chunks.text:
| Variable                                                                                                                              | Effect                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ARMORIQ_API_KEY`                                                                                                                     | The API key, if you pass none                                                                                                        |
| `ARMORIQ_BACKEND_URL` or `BACKEND_ENDPOINT`                                                                                           | The ArmorIQ backend. The SDK sends traces to `<backend>/v1/traces` and reads the policy from `<backend>/observability/policy/lease`. |
| `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY`                                                                                                               | `0`, `false`, `off`, `no`, or `disabled` turns tracing off for the process                                                           |
| `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORTER`                                                                                                               | `armoriq`, `external`, or `provider`. It overrides the option.                                                                       |
| `ARMORIQ_OTEL_CAPTURE_MODE`                                                                                                           | The local capture limit. It overrides the option.                                                                                    |
| `ARMORIQ_OTEL_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`                                          | The endpoint for `external` export                                                                                                   |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS`                                                                     | Headers for `external` export                                                                                                        |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT`, `ARMORIQ_OTEL_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_MS`                                   | The export time limit                                                                                                                |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CLIENT_KEY` (and the `_TRACES_` forms) | Custom CA and client certificate files for `external` export                                                                         |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`                                                                                                                   | The service name, if `service_name` is not set                                                                                       |
| `ARMORIQ_ENV`                                                                                                                         | The `deployment.environment` label on exported spans (default `unknown`)                                                             |

The `armoriq` export ignores the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables. Only `external` export reads them. Header values use URL encoding. The full rules for endpoints and headers are in [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership#settings-reference).

chunks.heading: What the SDK records
chunks.text:
The SDK adds these spans without code from you:

| Span name                                                                       | When                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `armoriq.agent.run`                                                             | The root span of the session                                                                             |
| `armoriq.intent.plan`                                                           | The plan                                                                                                 |
| `armoriq.policy.evaluate`                                                       | Each policy decision                                                                                     |
| `gen_ai.chat`                                                                   | Each model call                                                                                          |
| `armoriq.tool`, `mcp.execute`, `bash.execute`, `cli.execute`, `command.execute` | Tool and command work. Group operations by the `armoriq.operation.category` attribute, not by span name. |
| `armoriq.approval.wait`, `armoriq.delegation.wait`                              | A hold that waits for approval                                                                           |

See [What data is captured](/platform/observability/data-capture) for fields and [Data model](/platform/observability/data-model) for the attributes.

chunks.heading: How it behaves
chunks.text:
* **The SDK reads your organization policy first.** It fetches the capture policy with your API key. The first span waits for the answer for up to 5 seconds. If the policy is not available, the SDK records nothing until it is.
* **Failures are fail-open.** A tracing error never changes an allow, hold, or block result, and never raises into your code.
* **Closing is bounded.** `close()` makes one final send with a limit of 3 seconds.
* **No silent fallback.** If an `external` endpoint is missing or invalid, the SDK exports nothing and logs why. It does not use `localhost` or ArmorIQ instead.
* **Concurrent requests stay apart.** The SDK keeps context separate for each task and thread.

chunks.heading: Set Up OpenTelemetry Tracing
chunks.text:
This guide is for developers who already use the ArmorIQ SDK, or who are adding it to an agent. After you finish, each agent run sends one trace to ArmorIQ. A trace is the record of one run. It holds spans, and each span is one timed step, such as a policy decision, a model call, or a tool call. You write no span code and no flush code.

<Callout type="warn">
  This guide uses the current releases: Python SDK `armoriq-sdk` **0.8.17** and TypeScript SDK `@armoriq/sdk` **0.8.23**. Older SDKs use a legacy recorder that is not described here. To move from one, read [Migrate from the legacy recorder](/platform/observability/migration).
</Callout>

chunks.heading: What you need
chunks.text:
* An organization-scoped [ArmorIQ API key](/platform/api-keys/create-key).
* Python 3.10 to 3.13, or Node.js 18.19 or later (or 20.6 or later). The TypeScript LangChain and Strands adapters need Node.js 20 or later.
* The ArmorIQ SDK: `armoriq-sdk` 0.8.17 for Python, or `@armoriq/sdk` 0.8.23 for TypeScript.

<Tabs groupId="language" items="['Python', 'TypeScript']">
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```bash
    python -m pip install "armoriq-sdk==0.8.17"
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```bash
    npm install @armoriq/sdk@0.8.23
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

chunks.heading: Use ArmorIQ as you normally do
chunks.text:
Tracing is on by default. You do not add observability options, a tracer, or a flush call. This example uses the LangChain adapter. The Strands and Google ADK adapters work the same way. See [Framework support](/platform/observability/frameworks).

<Tabs groupId="language" items="['Python', 'TypeScript']">
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    from armoriq_sdk import ArmorIQClient
    from armoriq_sdk.integrations.langchain import ArmorIQLangChain

    # Once per process
    armoriq = ArmorIQLangChain(
        armoriq_client=ArmorIQClient(api_key=os.environ["ARMORIQ_API_KEY"]),
        mode="sdk",
    )

    # Per request
    handler = armoriq.for_user("alice@example.com", goal=user_message)
    agent_executor.invoke(
        {"input": user_message},
        config={"callbacks": [handler]},
    )
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { ArmorIQClient } from '@armoriq/sdk';
    import { ArmorIQLangChain } from '@armoriq/sdk/dist/integrations/langchain';

    // Once per process
    const armoriq = new ArmorIQLangChain({
      client: new ArmorIQClient({ apiKey: process.env.ARMORIQ_API_KEY! }),
      mode: 'sdk',
    });

    // Per request
    const handler = await armoriq.forUser('alice@example.com', { goal: userMessage });
    await agentExecutor.invoke(
      { input: userMessage },
      { callbacks: [handler] },
    );
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

That is all. The adapter does this for you:

| What happens                                                                               | When                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The SDK creates the trace and its root span                                                | At the start of the agent run                                                |
| The SDK adds spans for the plan, each policy decision, each model call, and each tool call | While the agent runs                                                         |
| The SDK ends the trace one time                                                            | When the run succeeds, fails, is cancelled, or times out                     |
| The SDK waits a short, fixed time for spans to send                                        | At the end of the run (up to 3 seconds in Python, 1.5 seconds in TypeScript) |

The SDK makes sure the trace ends one time only, even if the framework sends more than one end event. Telemetry never changes the result of the agent. If sending fails, the agent still returns its normal result.

chunks.heading: If you do not use a framework adapter
Check the first trace
chunks.text:
1. Run the agent once.
2. Open **Observability** in the ArmorIQ dashboard. The page is `/dashboard/observability`.
3. Find your session. Open the trace to see the plan, the policy decisions, and the tool work.

The dashboard polls every 30 seconds, so the trace can appear a short time after the run ends. If nothing appears, use [Troubleshooting](/platform/observability/troubleshooting).

chunks.heading: What the SDK does by itself
chunks.text:
* **It sends to ArmorIQ.** By default the SDK sends traces to `POST /v1/traces` on your ArmorIQ backend. This is the OTLP route. OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) is the standard way that OpenTelemetry tools send trace data over HTTP. The SDK signs in with your API key.
* **It asks your organization what to capture.** Before it records data, the SDK reads the capture policy for your organization. Your administrators set that policy. See [Organization controls](/platform/observability/organization-controls). If the policy is not available, the SDK records nothing.
* **It uses its own tracer provider.** A tracer provider is the object that creates spans and hands them to an exporter. The SDK builds a private one. It does not use or change the provider that your application may already have. To send traces somewhere else, or to use your own provider, see [Choose who exports your traces](/platform/observability/provider-ownership).

chunks.heading: Turn tracing off for one session
chunks.text:
<Tabs groupId="language" items="['Python', 'TypeScript']">
  <Tab value="Python">
    ```python
    session = client.start_session(SessionOptions(observability_enabled=False))
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    const session = client.startSession({ observability: { enabled: false } });
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

To turn tracing off for a whole process, set `ARMORIQ_OBSERVABILITY=off` in the environment. The values `0`, `false`, `off`, `no`, and `disabled` all work. Turning tracing off does not change any policy decision.
